metadata.note: The third and last of the three companies that merged in 1900 to form the Pere Marquette Railroad (alongside the Flint and Pere Marquette, see flint_pere_marquette_mainline.geojson, and the Chicago and West Michigan, see chicago_west_michigan_railway.geojson) -- and arguably the most important omission, since it's the direct ancestor of the Detroit-Grand Rapids passenger corridor. The Detroit, Lansing and Michigan Railroad was foreclosed and reorganized in Dec 1876 as the Detroit, Lansing and Northern Railroad (DL&N), running Detroit-Lansing-Ionia-Greenville-Howard City, with later branches to Stanton and (via Edmore) to Big Rapids. In 1888 the company built a more direct route, the Grand Rapids, Lansing and Detroit, from Grand Ledge to Grand Rapids -- giving Detroit its own direct line to Grand Rapids alongside the older Howard City route. DL&N went into receivership Apr 1 1896 and was reorganized Jan 1 1897 as the Detroit, Grand Rapids and Western Railroad (DGR&W), which along the way had also absorbed the Saginaw Valley and St. Louis, Saginaw and Grand Rapids, and Saginaw and Western railroads. DGR&W was folded into the new Pere Marquette Railroad in 1900. Geometry is a real-town waypoint approximation, straight-line segments between documented stations -- NOT digitized from period track maps. COLOR NOTE: the Pere Marquette-era (1900-1947) features here use #9C6644, matching every other Pere Marquette-branded feature on this map.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit,_Lansing_and_Northern_Railroad (DL&N formed Dec 1876 from the foreclosed Detroit, Lansing and Michigan Railroad; ran Detroit-Lansing-Ionia-Greenville-Howard City, later branches to Stanton and via Edmore to Big Rapids; operated over the Saginaw Valley and St. Louis Railroad; built the Grand Rapids, Lansing and Detroit from Grand Ledge to Grand Rapids in 1888 for a more direct connection; receivership Apr 1 1896, reorganized as Detroit, Grand Rapids and Western Railroad Jan 1 1897, also absorbing the Saginaw and Grand Rapids and Saginaw and Western railroads; folded into the new Pere Marquette Railroad 1900
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Exact discontinuation date for passenger service on either corridor (approximated here at Amtrak's May 1 1971 creation, matching this map's convention for Michigan lines not selected by Amtrak, not independently confirmed); precise frequency for any era, all estimated; the Stanton and Big Rapids/Edmore branches are not separately modeled here.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
